newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - DELFOOD YR SHR SEEN UP ON BAD 1995.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - DELFOOD YR SHR SEEN UP ON BAD 1995.

text.p: South African food group Del Monte Royal Foods Ltd is set to post a jump in year earnings per share, but analysts said the figures were coming after a bad performance in 1995.
Delfood is expected to report earnings per share of 52 cents, up from 42.6 cents last time, with the dividend hiked to 19-22 cents, up from 16.0 cents last time.
"The figures are a rise, but it is on the back of their shocking results last year," said one analyst, who declined to be named.
Delfood is set to bring out its results on February 14.

In 1995 the firm's fruit operation, which produces most of its pineapples in Kenya, was hit by a strong Kenyan shilling. The group also suffered from costs associated with an attempted acquisition of a major European food business that failed to materialise.
However, this year the shilling has been stable, as has the peso in the Phillipines -- another important area of fruit production. Pineapple prices have also been stronger in 1996 than in 1995.

Analysts said the group's beverages unit had performed well, but that the fruit operations were more difficult to judge due to their diverse spread of operations, both geographically and by type of fruit.
"The fruit market generally is soft but it is a very difficult company to analyse as they are so diverse and spread across the board," said another analyst.
The group is aiming to crack a magic formula of low cost fruit production in developing countries with sales to the more developed world -- giving it healthy margins.
But analysts said the firm had yet to break decisively into the key European market.

Last June the firm warned that competitive pressures in Europe were still strong, but that it had maintained or improved its market share in the first half of the year and recent price increases seemed to be holding.
"The question is really whether they can do effective retailing, marketing and distribution in Europe," one analyst said, adding that the jury remained out on the success of the group there.
